Add posterior draws from a model to a data object

Source: R/add-methods.R
add_fitted_samples.Rd

Adds draws from the posterior distribution of model to the data object using one of fitted_samples(), predicted_samples(), or posterior_samples().

Usage

add_fitted_samples(
  data,
  model,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  chains = NULL
)

add_predicted_samples(data, model, ..., n_draws = NULL, seed = NULL)

add_posterior_samples(
  data,
  model,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  chains = NULL
)

add_smooth_samples(
  data,
  model,
  ...,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  select = NULL,
  chains = NULL
)

Arguments

data

a data frame or tibble to which the posterior draws will be added.

model

a fitted GAM (or GAM-like) object for which a posterior draw method exists.

...

arguments are passed to the posterior draw function, currently one of fitted_samples(), predicted_samples(), or posterior_samples(). n_draws and seed are already specified here as arguments and are also passed on to the posterior sampling function.

n_draws

positive integer; total retained draws across all chains. Required when generating draws. With method = "user", the supplied matrix determines the count; an explicit count must agree with its rows.

seed

numeric; a value to seed the random number generator.

chains

positive integer or NULL; number of chains. NULL uses one chain, or the chain mapping in supplied draws. n_draws must be divisible by chains. Burn-in is applied separately to each MH chain.

select

character; select which smooth's posterior to draw from. The default, NULL, means the posteriors of all smooths in model will be returned using the same joint coefficient draws. If supplied, a vector of smooth terms.

Examples

load_mgcv()

df <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, seed = 42)

m <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = df, method = "REML")

# add fitted samples (posterior draws of the expected value of the response)
# note that there are 800 rows in the output: 400 data by `n_draws = 2` samples.
df |>
  add_fitted_samples(m, n_draws = 2, seed = 84)
#> # A tibble: 800 × 14
#>        y    x0     x1    x2    x3     f    f0    f1     f2    f3  .row .draw
#>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <int> <int>
#>  1  2.99 0.915 0.0227 0.909 0.402  1.62 0.529  1.05 0.0397     0     1     1
#>  2  2.99 0.915 0.0227 0.909 0.402  1.62 0.529  1.05 0.0397     0     1     2
#>  3  4.70 0.937 0.513  0.900 0.432  3.25 0.393  2.79 0.0630     0     2     1
#>  4  4.70 0.937 0.513  0.900 0.432  3.25 0.393  2.79 0.0630     0     2     2
#>  5 13.9  0.286 0.631  0.192 0.664 13.5  1.57   3.53 8.41       0     3     1
#>  6 13.9  0.286 0.631  0.192 0.664 13.5  1.57   3.53 8.41       0     3     2
#>  7  5.71 0.830 0.419  0.532 0.182  6.12 1.02   2.31 2.79       0     4     1
#>  8  5.71 0.830 0.419  0.532 0.182  6.12 1.02   2.31 2.79       0     4     2
#>  9  7.63 0.642 0.879  0.522 0.838 10.4  1.80   5.80 2.76       0     5     1
#> 10  7.63 0.642 0.879  0.522 0.838 10.4  1.80   5.80 2.76       0     5     2
#> # ℹ 790 more rows
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: .parameter <chr>, .fitted <dbl>

# add posterior draws from smooth s(x2)
df |>
  add_smooth_samples(m, n_draws = 2, seed = 2, select= "s(x2)")
#> # A tibble: 800 × 15
#>        y    x0     x1    x2    x3     f    f0    f1     f2    f3  .row .smooth
#>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <int> <chr>

#>  5 13.9  0.286 0.631  0.192 0.664 13.5  1.57   3.53 8.41       0     3 s(x2)  
#>  6 13.9  0.286 0.631  0.192 0.664 13.5  1.57   3.53 8.41       0     3 s(x2)  
#>  7  5.71 0.830 0.419  0.532 0.182  6.12 1.02   2.31 2.79       0     4 s(x2)  
#>  8  5.71 0.830 0.419  0.532 0.182  6.12 1.02   2.31 2.79       0     4 s(x2)  
#>  9  7.63 0.642 0.879  0.522 0.838 10.4  1.80   5.80 2.76       0     5 s(x2)
